events.scenario_brief: Maya receives approval to pay the fare difference for the Cleveland return change after the client moves Thursday’s closeout to 4:00 p.m. The later nonstop gives her more time to leave the hospital campus, retrieve her stored luggage if needed, and reach the airport without rushing, though it gets her back to Atlanta later in the evening. The original rear window seat cannot be carried over automatically, but the new flight still has one rear window and several aisle seats available. Remaining items are completing the airline change, selecting the best available seat, updating the calendar, and saving the new receipt for the trip file.

events.continuity_hook: Starts the next work-travel episode after the Cleveland trip is wrapped up.
events.interaction_goal: Frame the Minneapolis trip, identify workable flight windows and hotel areas, and list the client details needed before Maya requests approval.
events.scenario_brief: After returning from Cleveland, Maya gets a September request for an onsite training and workflow review with a Minneapolis client. The rough plan is to fly from Atlanta on Monday, run sessions Tuesday and Wednesday, and return Thursday after a possible client debrief. Atlanta to Minneapolis has several nonstop options, while one-stop itineraries save little and add travel risk. The main uncertainty is whether the work will be at the downtown office near the medical center or at a suburban training site, which will determine whether a downtown hotel, suburban hotel, or airport-area hotel makes sense. Remaining items are the exact site address, Tuesday start time, Thursday end time, nightly hotel ceiling, and whether a coworker needs to coordinate arrival timing.

events.continuity_hook: Continues Minneapolis planning once the worksite and meeting times are confirmed.
events.interaction_goal: Compare the main Minneapolis flight-and-hotel combinations and choose the practical approval-ready plan.
events.scenario_brief: The Minneapolis client confirms that the sessions will be at the downtown medical center office, with an 8:30 a.m. Tuesday start, a full Wednesday schedule, and a Thursday debrief expected to end around noon. The cleanest outbound is a Monday late-morning nonstop that lands with enough time for hotel check-in and prep. For Thursday, an early-afternoon nonstop is possible but tight if the debrief runs long, while a late-afternoon nonstop leaves a calmer margin. Hotel choices include a downtown property close to the office with strong guest ratings, on-site dining, and paid breakfast; a suite-style hotel with included breakfast but a longer walk or short rideshare; and a cheaper airport-area property that would make both client mornings less predictable.

events.continuity_hook: Moves the Minneapolis work trip from comparison into booking while the approved flights and hotel are still available.
events.interaction_goal: Finalize the Minneapolis flights, hotel, seat choices, room request, local transportation notes, and confirmation records.
events.scenario_brief: Maya’s manager approves the Monday late-morning nonstop to Minneapolis, the Thursday late-afternoon nonstop home, and the downtown hotel as long as the room remains cancellable. The fare and hotel rate are still available, and the hotel confirms a quiet-room request can be added but not guaranteed. Breakfast is not included, though there is an early cafe in the lobby and several casual dinner options within walking distance. Seat maps show rear window seats open on both flights, with forward seats mostly aisle or middle. Remaining items are completing the booking, selecting seats, adding the room request, noting airport-to-hotel transportation, and saving confirmations for reimbursement.

events.continuity_hook: Starts a new family leisure episode after the September work trip planning is handled.
events.interaction_goal: Frame the D.C. family weekend, compare airport and hotel-area tradeoffs, and identify what Maya needs to confirm with her spouse.
events.scenario_brief: With the school fall-break calendar settled, Maya starts exploring a three-night family museum weekend in Washington, D.C. with her spouse and child. They are considering a Friday departure and Monday return, hoping to arrive early enough for an easy first evening and return before Monday night gets too late. Nonstops from Atlanta to Reagan National are the most convenient for the city, while Dulles and Baltimore options sometimes price lower but add longer ground transfers. Hotel areas under consideration include Penn Quarter, Capitol Hill, Dupont Circle, and Arlington near Metro. The family wants easy access to Smithsonian museums, casual dinners, and enough room comfort for three people, while weighing included breakfast against being closer to the first two sightseeing days. Remaining items are exact dates, nightly budget, how much Metro walking feels reasonable, and whether any timed museum or monument plans should drive the hotel area.

events.continuity_hook: Continues the D.C. family weekend after the dates and airport priorities are clarified.
events.interaction_goal: Narrow the D.C. flights and hotel choice to one family-ready plan with the main tradeoffs clearly summarized.
events.scenario_brief: Maya’s spouse confirms the Friday-to-Monday fall-break window and wants the simplest city access over chasing the lowest fare. The leading flight plan is a late-morning nonstop from Atlanta to Reagan National and an early-afternoon nonstop home, while cheaper Dulles and Baltimore itineraries add transfer time and make the first or last day less smooth. The hotel shortlist has narrowed to a Penn Quarter hotel with strong ratings, walkable museum access, and many restaurants nearby but paid breakfast; a Capitol Hill suite-style option with included breakfast and more space but fewer nearby dinner choices; and an Arlington hotel with a lower nightly rate and larger rooms but Metro rides for most sightseeing. Remaining decisions are whether downtown convenience outweighs breakfast and room size, whether the Reagan fare is worth booking now, and whether to hold a cancellable hotel while they finalize museum plans.

events.continuity_hook: Follows the narrowed D.C. family plan after Maya’s spouse favored Reagan National and downtown convenience over lower-cost airport or suburban options.
events.interaction_goal: Turn the D.C. shortlist into a bookable family plan, including flights, hotel hold or booking choice, seat layout, and the breakfast-versus-location tradeoff.
events.scenario_brief: Maya and her spouse settle on the simplest D.C. access plan for the fall-break weekend: a Friday late-morning nonstop from Atlanta to Reagan National, a Monday early-afternoon nonstop back to Atlanta, and the Penn Quarter hotel because it keeps the first two museum days walkable and has strong guest ratings with plenty of nearby casual restaurants. The tradeoff is that breakfast is paid rather than included, and the downtown rate is higher than the Arlington option. What remains unresolved is whether to book the airfare immediately, hold the cancellable hotel while timed-entry plans firm up, and choose seats that keep the family together without giving up a window entirely.

events.continuity_hook: Handles the practical D.C. follow-up after the main flights and hotel are in place but before the fall-break weekend begins.
events.interaction_goal: Confirm the D.C. trip still works after the minor flight change and tighten the seat, arrival, hotel, and first-evening logistics.
events.scenario_brief: The D.C. flights are booked and the Penn Quarter hotel is held at a cancellable rate. A minor airline schedule change moves the Monday return slightly later but still keeps the family home before the evening gets too late. The hotel confirms baggage storage but cannot guarantee early check-in, and a better three-seat row with a window has opened farther back on the outbound. The family now has a Saturday morning museum entry, making the downtown hotel even more useful despite the lack of included breakfast. Remaining details are accepting the schedule change, switching seats, adding the bag-storage note, and setting a simple arrival-evening dinner plan near the hotel.

events.continuity_hook: Starts the next work-related travel episode once the family fall-break planning is effectively settled.
events.interaction_goal: Frame the Denver training trip, identify reasonable flight windows and hotel areas, and list the details Maya needs before preparing an approval request.
events.scenario_brief: After the D.C. weekend, Maya is asked to attend a three-day product training in Denver in mid-November. She would travel solo from Atlanta, with sessions expected Tuesday through Thursday at a downtown training center and a Monday evening reception that may or may not be required. Atlanta has several nonstop Denver options, while one-stop itineraries do not save enough to justify extra risk in late-fall weather. Hotel choices will likely center on the training hotel, nearby downtown properties, or a cheaper airport-area stay that would complicate the early sessions. Still unresolved are the exact training-center address, whether Monday evening attendance is expected, Thursday end time, nightly hotel ceiling, and whether any coworkers want to coordinate arrival timing.

events.continuity_hook: Continues Denver planning after the training location and schedule are firm enough to compare concrete flight-and-hotel combinations.
events.interaction_goal: Choose an approval-ready Denver plan by balancing the nonstop flight timing, return-day risk, hotel convenience, breakfast, and cancellation terms.
events.scenario_brief: The Denver training details are confirmed: the site is downtown near Union Station, Tuesday registration starts at 8:15 a.m., Wednesday is a full lab day, and Thursday should end around 3:00 p.m. The Monday reception is useful but not mandatory. A Monday morning nonstop from Atlanta would land with enough time for check-in and light prep, while traveling Sunday would add an unnecessary hotel night. For the return, a Thursday evening nonstop is workable if the last session ends on time, while Friday morning would be calmer but adds cost. The hotel comparison now includes the official training hotel with strong ratings and on-site dining but paid breakfast, a nearby suite-style property with included breakfast and a longer walk, and an airport hotel that is cheaper but impractical for the first morning.

events.continuity_hook: Moves the Denver training trip from comparison to booking while the approved flights and hotel rate are still available.
events.interaction_goal: Finalize the Denver flights, hotel, seats, room request, transportation notes, and reimbursement records.
events.scenario_brief: Maya’s manager approves the Monday morning nonstop to Denver, the Thursday evening nonstop home, and the official training hotel as long as the room remains cancellable through the company deadline. The hotel rate is still available, has a solid guest rating, and offers on-site dining, though breakfast is not included. Seat maps show rear window seats available on both flights, with forward seats mostly middle or aisle. The remaining tasks are booking before the fare changes, selecting the best available windows, adding a quiet-room request, noting airport-to-hotel transportation, and saving confirmations and receipts for reimbursement.

events.continuity_hook: Handles the final Denver pre-trip check after booking, prompted by a small flight schedule change and late-fall weather considerations.
events.interaction_goal: Decide whether any Denver adjustments are needed and update the final flight, hotel, seat, and departure-timing checklist.
events.scenario_brief: A week before the Denver training, the flights and official hotel are booked. The airline moves the Monday outbound 20 minutes earlier, which still works but makes the Decatur-to-airport departure slightly earlier than Maya first planned. The hotel cancellation deadline is approaching, and the training organizer confirms Tuesday morning registration is firm but Thursday’s closing lab should still end by 3:00 p.m. A light snow forecast in Denver makes the nonstop routing and downtown hotel more valuable than switching to a cheaper airport-area option. Remaining items are accepting the schedule change, confirming the selected window seats, keeping the hotel, and updating the calendar with a more conservative Monday airport-arrival buffer.

versions.boundary_condition: This is a soft preference: Delta is favored only among otherwise suitable options and may coexist with other acceptable preferred carriers.
versions.condition: When choosing among flight carriers and Delta is available while also satisfying the trip's schedule, route, price, and stop constraints.
versions.default_action: Search for or present Delta options as part of the preferred carrier set, and favor Delta when it is otherwise comparable to alternatives.
versions.exception_condition: Use another acceptable carrier when Delta is unavailable, materially worse, or does not meet the current trip constraints.
versions.name: soft_delta_preferred_carrier
versions.preference_value: Delta is a preferred airline to include in the flight shortlist, but not an exclusive carrier requirement.
versions.scope_condition: Maya's recurring work, conference, and personal air trips departing from or returning to Atlanta when Delta appears among feasible carrier options.

versions.boundary_condition: Applies only to seat location. If seat selection is unavailable at booking or is deferred until check-in, note that limitation and try to secure a window seat at the earliest available time.
versions.condition: When booking or selecting seats for flights where a seat location preference can be applied.
versions.default_action: Prefer or request a window seat by default.
versions.exception_condition: Use a different seat only if the user specifies another seat preference, needs a different seating arrangement, or no acceptable window seat is available.
versions.name: prefers_window_seat_on_flights
versions.scope_condition: Maya's own seat on commercial flights for solo or family travel whenever seat location can be selected at booking, later management, or check-in.

versions.boundary_condition: Treat as a soft default; if true afternoon return departures are unavailable, limited, or unattractive, consider options close to afternoon.
versions.condition: When booking or comparing round-trip flights and selecting the return-leg departure time.
versions.default_action: Search for return-flight options departing in the afternoon and present those first when available.
versions.exception_condition: Do not apply as a universal outbound-leg rule; one supporting dialogue separately used a morning outbound while still preferring an afternoon return.
versions.name: afternoon_return_departure_preference
versions.preference_value: Prefer the return flight to depart in the afternoon.
versions.scope_condition: Return legs of round trips back home after client visits, conferences, spouse weekends, or family trips when the return departure time has flexibility.

versions.boundary_condition: Do not infer that the user always wants nonstop first, wants a layover for price reasons, or wants to add a stop to break up a long route unless the current request says so.
versions.condition: When evaluating flight itineraries where a connection is acceptable, necessary, or being considered.
versions.default_action: Favor itineraries with at most one short layover; ask before selecting itineraries with multiple layovers or a long layover.
versions.exception_condition: Override this default if the user explicitly requests nonstop only, requests a longer stopover, or prioritizes schedule, availability, price, or another constraint over layover count or layover duration.
versions.name: flight_single_short_layover_preference
versions.preference_value: Prefers connecting itineraries with no more than one layover, and for any layover to be short enough for a comfortable transfer rather than prolonged.
versions.scope_condition: Work and personal flight itineraries where a connection is acceptable, necessary, or under consideration, especially on domestic and simple international routes.

versions.boundary_condition: This is a soft customer/review-rating default, not an exact 4-star-only rule, not a hotel-class-star requirement, and not a reusable 4.5-star or 3.5-star threshold by itself.
versions.condition: When searching for hotels and a Google rating, review score, or similar customer-facing rating is available, especially for nice, upscale, resort-style, or high-rated stays.
versions.default_action: Filter or rank toward hotels with customer-facing ratings of at least 4.0 stars and report the rating source when known.
versions.exception_condition: If the user specifies a different threshold, prioritizes a budget stay with an explicit lower floor such as 3.5 stars, asks for the cheapest option regardless of quality, only suitable options fall below 4.0, or the rating metric is unclear, follow or clarify the current trip-specific instruction instead of hard-enforcing the 4.0 default.
versions.name: hotel_four_star_customer_rating_floor
versions.preference_value: Prefer hotels with clearly good customer-facing ratings, normally at least 4.0 stars, while treating higher ratings such as 4.5 as a bonus and lower stated floors as trip-specific exceptions.
versions.scope_condition: Hotel searches for Maya's solo work stays and family leisure stays when a customer-facing hotel rating is available.

versions.boundary_condition: Use this as a soft preference, not an absolute requirement, because the evidence ranges from a direct requirement to a tentative request and a later verification question.
versions.condition: When evaluating or booking a hotel, treat free breakfast as a recurring included-service preference.
versions.default_action: Prioritize or verify hotels with free breakfast when available; if breakfast is not listed, ask or check rather than assuming it is included.
versions.exception_condition: Do not reject an otherwise suitable hotel solely for lacking free breakfast unless the user explicitly makes it required in the current booking; do not infer a full or high-quality breakfast requirement unless stated.
versions.name: prefer_included_hotel_breakfast
versions.preference_value: Prefer hotels that include free breakfast.
versions.scope_condition: Hotel comparisons for work or family stays of more than one night, especially when mornings are early or the itinerary is busy.

versions.boundary_condition: Do not infer specific cuisine, star rating, bar service, kid-friendliness, downtown location, ski access, or wooded setting unless stated for the current trip.
versions.condition: When searching for, comparing, or summarizing hotel options.
versions.default_action: Mention on-site or nearby restaurant availability and use convenient dining access as a soft tie-breaker rather than a hard filter.
versions.exception_condition: Do not apply if the user explicitly deprioritizes dining access or if stronger current-trip constraints override it.
versions.name: hotel_restaurant_access
versions.preference_value: Hotels with on-site or nearby restaurant access, with restaurant availability noted during comparisons.
versions.scope_condition: Hotel searches where Maya may arrive after a workday, attend a conference, or rely on rideshare instead of having a car, making on-site or nearby restaurant access useful.
